nodes.label: Dual MCP implementation pattern
nodes.rationale: Two separate MCP implementations exist: mcp_server.py (fastmcp standalone on :8006) and main.py (fastapi-mcp auto-exposing FastAPI routes). This provides both rich bundled tool access for AI assistants and auto-generated tool coverage without code duplication.

nodes.label: Endpoint enum as extensibility pattern
nodes.rationale: The Endpoint enum centralizes all upstream query strings so adding a new equity endpoint only requires adding one enum value with no other changes. This is an intentional extensibility design.

nodes.label: Market Data Dict Pattern
nodes.rationale: All data sources are aggregated into a single typed dict keyed by source name (mmi, us_fg, quotes, metals, ipos, ncds, bonds, timestamp). This uniform dict is passed to both formatter and summary, enabling each consumer to pick only what it needs without requiring changes to function signatures when new sources are added.

nodes.label: Trusted Rating Agency Filter Pattern
nodes.rationale: Both ncd.py and secondary_bonds.py share the same TRUSTED_AGENCIES set (ICRA, CRISIL, CARE), _RATING_RANKS map, and MINIMUM_RATING_RANK=7 constant (A- and above), and near-identical _is_trusted_a_series helpers. This is a deliberate quality filter ensuring only investment-grade bonds from reputable agencies are shown to users.

nodes.label: Equity Proxy Endpoint Enum
nodes.rationale: Using an Endpoint enum mapping short names to full upstream query strings means adding a new equity endpoint only requires adding a value to the enum — no other code changes needed. This reduces friction and limits the blast radius of changes.

nodes.label: Dual MCP Implementation Strategy
nodes.rationale: Two MCP implementations exist: mcp_server.py (standalone fastmcp-based, rich per-company tools, company_id identifier) and main.py (auto-exposes FastAPI routes via fastapi-mcp). This allows both rich programmatic tool access and automatic REST-to-MCP bridging.

nodes.label: Add New Data Source Pattern
nodes.rationale: New data sources follow a four-step pattern: create source module, register in fetcher, add formatting, optionally expose as endpoint/tool. This convention enforces consistent extensibility.
